I wrote /app/bin/boards.py and ran it on /app/data, which produced /app/out/boards.json. Both checks pass.

- python tools/check_boards.py: all 265 of 265 boards match the approved ones, and the service dates match.
- python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .: 4 tests ran and all passed.

I wrote /app/STATUS.json with "status": "success". The script uses only the standard library, and I didn't touch /app/data, /app/docs, /app/tests or /app/tools.

I only checked the script against the current feed and the four small test feeds. The script follows the numbered rules in /app/docs rather than anything specific to the current files, but I haven't run it on other feeds or dates.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | head -100; cat docs/overview.md; wc -c docs/*
cd /app/docs; cat feed.md service.md trips.md boards.md output.md changelog.md
cd /app; for f in data/*; do echo == $f; head -4 $f; wc -l $f; done; cat tools/check_boards.py | head -40; sed -n 1,50p tests/test_boards.py
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/boards.py data out/boards.json && python tools/check_boards.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -15

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/boards.py implementing the documented rules; ran it on /app/data to /app/out/boards.json. check_boards.py matches 265 of 265 boards and the 4 unit tests pass."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
